options.text: Numbness in groin/buttocks area or loss of bladder/bowel control
Severe weakness in both legs or spreading numbness
Chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or heart palpitations

CERVICAL_006.text: Are your symptoms worse when holding your arms overhead?

HIP_005.text: Is your pain worse with deep hip flexion (like bringing knee to chest)?

THORACIC_003.text: Is your pain worse with deep breathing?

THORACIC_004.text: Do you notice a visible curve in your spine?

HEAD_004.text: Is your vertigo triggered by head movements (like looking up or rolling over)?

SYSTEMIC_003.text: Is your morning stiffness lasting more than 60 minutes?

SYSTEMIC_004.text: Are your joint symptoms symmetric (affecting both sides equally)?

SYSTEMIC_005.text: Do you have trouble sleeping or unrefreshing sleep?

NEURO_003.text: Have your movements become slower than before?

NEURO_005.text: Are your symptoms only on one side of your body?

NEURO_006.text: Do your symptoms come and go (relapsing and remitting)?

NEURO_007.text: Have you noticed any vision problems?

GENERAL_PAIN_001.text: Is your pain worse at night?

GENERAL_PAIN_002.text: Does your pain improve with rest?

GENERAL_PAIN_003.text: Have you had similar episodes before?

PELVIS_002.text: Do you have pain in your buttock that radiates down your leg?

PELVIS_003.text: Is your pain related to your menstrual cycle?

PELVIS_004.text: Do you have pain or difficulty with urination?

PELVIS_005.text: Do you feel heaviness or pressure in your pelvic area?

PELVIS_006.text: Is your pain worse when sitting for long periods?

LOWER_LEG_001.text: Is your pain in your calf muscle?

LOWER_LEG_002.text: Is your pain along the front of your shin?

LOWER_LEG_003.text: Did your pain start during running or exercise?

LOWER_LEG_004.text: Do you have cramping or tightness in your calf during walking?

LOWER_LEG_005.text: Is there swelling, redness, or warmth in your calf?

LOWER_LEG_006.text: Does your pain get worse with activity and improve with rest?

CARDIO_001.text: Do you get short of breath with activities that didn't used to bother you?

CARDIO_002.text: Do you have a chronic cough or wheeze?

CARDIO_003.text: Do you have swelling in your ankles or legs?

CARDIO_004.text: Have you had a recent heart attack or heart surgery?

CARDIO_005.text: Do you get leg pain when walking that goes away with rest?

CARDIO_006.text: Do you feel unusually tired even after rest?

SHOULDER_011.text: Is your pain on the very top of your shoulder (where shoulder meets collarbone)?

SHOULDER_012.text: Does reaching across your body (like touching opposite shoulder) cause pain?

SHOULDER_013.text: Is your pain worse when lying on the affected shoulder at night?

SHOULDER_014.text: Can you see or feel your shoulder blade sticking out abnormally?

SHOULDER_015.text: Is your pain in your chest/front of shoulder near the armpit?

SHOULDER_016.text: Do you have weakness when pushing (like doing a push-up)?

SHOULDER_017.text: Did your pain come on suddenly and severely?

CERVICAL_007.text: Do your symptoms affect BOTH arms (not just one side)?

CERVICAL_008.text: Have you noticed problems with walking, balance, or coordination?

CERVICAL_009.text: Have you noticed clumsiness with your hands (dropping things, difficulty with buttons)?

CERVICAL_010.text: Is your pain at the back of your head (base of skull)?

CERVICAL_011.text: Do you have shooting or electric shock-like pain?

CERVICAL_012.text: Do you feel grinding or crunching when moving your neck?

CERVICAL_013.text: Has your neck problem lasted more than 3 months?

CERVICAL_014.text: Is your pain just in your neck WITHOUT arm symptoms?

NEURO_008.text: Did your symptoms start in childhood?

NEURO_009.text: Do you have muscle stiffness or spasticity (tight, hard to move)?

NEURO_010.text: Is your weakness getting progressively worse over months?

NEURO_011.text: Do you have involuntary jerky or dance-like movements (chorea)?

NEURO_012.text: Does your weakness get worse with repeated activity and improve with rest?

NEURO_013.text: Do you have drooping eyelids or double vision?

NEURO_014.text: Did your weakness start in your legs and spread upward over days/weeks?

NEURO_016.text: Do you have a tremor mainly when reaching for objects (not at rest)?

NEURO_017.text: Did you have a recent head injury or trauma?

NEURO_018.text: Do you have involuntary sustained muscle contractions causing abnormal postures?

NEURO_019.text: Did you have a spinal cord injury (trauma, accident)?

ELBOW_007.text: Do you have swelling at the back of your elbow (pointy part)?

ELBOW_008.text: Is your pain worse with throwing or overhead sports?

ELBOW_009.text: Is your pain in your forearm (between elbow and wrist)?

ELBOW_010.text: Is your pain worse when rotating your forearm palm-down (pronation)?

ELBOW_011.text: Do you feel grinding or crunching when moving your elbow?

ELBOW_012.text: Do you have difficulty fully straightening your elbow?

ELBOW_013.text: Have you had recent elbow surgery or fracture?

WRIST_007.text: Is the pain on the back (top) of your wrist?

WRIST_008.text: Is the pain on the palm side of your wrist?

WRIST_009.text: Is your pain on the pinky side of your wrist?

WRIST_010.text: Can you see or feel a bump or lump on your wrist?

WRIST_011.text: Can you NOT fully straighten the tip of one of your fingers?

WRIST_012.text: Can you NOT bend/curl the tip of one of your fingers?

WRIST_013.text: Is your pain at the base of your thumb?

WRIST_014.text: Does your thumb feel unstable or give way?

WRIST_015.text: Is one of your fingers progressively curling towards your palm?

WRIST_016.text: Have you had a wrist fracture or been in a cast recently?

WRIST_017.text: Is your pain in the snuffbox area (hollow at base of thumb on back of hand)?

SYSTEMIC_006.text: Do you feel significantly worse after physical or mental exertion (post-exertional malaise)?

SYSTEMIC_007.text: Do you have burning or shooting pain that seems out of proportion to the injury?

SYSTEMIC_008.text: Does even light touch cause pain (allodynia)?

SYSTEMIC_009.text: Do you notice color or temperature changes in the affected limb?

SYSTEMIC_010.text: Are your joints unusually flexible (can you touch your thumb to your forearm)?

SYSTEMIC_011.text: Do you have a history of frequent joint dislocations or sprains?

SYSTEMIC_012.text: Do you have very stretchy or fragile skin that bruises easily?

SYSTEMIC_013.text: Does your back stiffness improve with exercise but worsen with rest?

SYSTEMIC_014.text: Do you have psoriasis (skin condition with red, scaly patches)?

SYSTEMIC_015.text: Do you have swollen, sausage-like fingers or toes (dactylitis)?

SYSTEMIC_016.text: Have you had fractures from minor trauma or noticed you are getting shorter?

FOOT_007.text: Is your big toe drifting towards your other toes with a bony bump on the side?

FOOT_008.text: Is your big toe stiff and painful when you try to bend it upward?

FOOT_009.text: Do you have one or more toes that are permanently bent in a claw-like position?

FOOT_010.text: Are you a child or teenager with heel pain after sports?

FOOT_011.text: Did you injure your big toe by jamming it or bending it back too far?

FOOT_012.text: Is your pain under the ball of your foot at the base of your big toe?

FOOT_013.text: Is your pain on the outer (lateral) side of your midfoot?

FOOT_014.text: Do you have burning, tingling, or numbness on the bottom of your foot?

FOOT_015.text: Did you have a twisting injury and now cannot put weight on your midfoot?

FOOT_016.text: Do you have a flat arch that has developed or gotten worse over time?

DIFF_KNE_001.text: Sit on a chair and try to straighten your leg fully. Can you lock it completely straight?
DIFF_KNE_001.patient_guidance: Sit on the edge of a chair. Slowly straighten your knee as far as it will go. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_001.clinical_note: Extension deficit suggests arthrofibrosis, meniscal block, or extensor mechanism injury

DIFF_KNE_002.text: Squat halfway down, keeping your feet flat. Does your knee feel like it might give way or buckle?
DIFF_KNE_002.patient_guidance: Hold onto a counter or wall for support. Bend your knees to about half-squat depth. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_002.clinical_note: Giving way during squat suggests ligament insufficiency or patellar instability

DIFF_KNE_003.text: Walk up 3 stairs slowly. Where exactly do you feel the pain?
DIFF_KNE_003.patient_guidance: Use a handrail for safety. Walk up 3 steps at a normal pace. Notice exactly where the pain is. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.

options.text: Above the knee / front of thigh

DIFF_KNE_003.clinical_note: Pain location during stair climbing discriminates anterior (PFP/tendon) vs medial (pes anserine/MCL) vs lateral (ITBS/LCL)

DIFF_KNE_004.text: Stand on your injured leg only for 10 seconds. Could you do it without your knee buckling?
DIFF_KNE_004.patient_guidance: Stand near a wall for safety. Lift your good leg off the ground and balance on the injured leg for up to 10 seconds. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_004.clinical_note: Single-leg stance failure suggests significant instability or weight-bearing intolerance

DIFF_KNE_005.text: Lie on your back and try to lift your straight leg about 30cm off the bed. Can you do it?
DIFF_KNE_005.patient_guidance: Lie flat on your back. Keep your knee completely straight and lift your whole leg about a foot off the surface. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_005.clinical_note: Straight leg raise failure is pathognomonic for extensor mechanism disruption (quad/patellar tendon rupture)

DIFF_KNE_006.text: Sit on a chair, then stand up and sit back down 5 times. How does your knee feel?
DIFF_KNE_006.patient_guidance: Use a sturdy chair. Stand up fully and sit back down 5 times at a comfortable pace. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_006.clinical_note: Sit-to-stand test assesses functional knee loading capacity

DIFF_KNE_007.text: Try to bend your knee as far as you can (heel towards buttock). How far can you go?
DIFF_KNE_007.patient_guidance: You can do this sitting or lying down. Bend your knee bringing your heel towards your buttock. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.

options.text: Almost there but a little short

DIFF_KNE_007.clinical_note: ROM limitation severity helps distinguish arthrofibrosis/effusion from muscular/pain-limited restriction

DIFF_KNE_008.text: Does your knee make a clicking, popping, or grinding sound when you bend and straighten it?
DIFF_KNE_008.clinical_note: Crepitus/clicking suggests chondromalacia, plica, or meniscal pathology

DIFF_KNE_009.text: Does your knee ever get stuck or lock in one position, where you can't straighten or bend it for a moment?
DIFF_KNE_009.clinical_note: True locking = meniscal/loose body; pseudo-locking = plica, pain inhibition

DIFF_KNE_010.text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of your injury?
DIFF_KNE_010.clinical_note: Audible pop strongly suggests ACL tear (~70% sensitivity); less common in PCL, patellar dislocation

DIFF_KNE_011.text: Did your knee swell up within the first 2 hours after the injury?
DIFF_KNE_011.clinical_note: Rapid hemarthrosis (<2h) suggests ACL tear, patellar dislocation, or fracture

DIFF_KNE_012.text: Is the pain worse when you first get up in the morning, then gradually improves as you move around?
DIFF_KNE_012.clinical_note: Morning stiffness <30min = OA pattern; >30min suggests inflammatory arthritis

DIFF_KNE_013.text: Where is the pain located most of the time?

options.text: Below the knee on the shin bone

DIFF_KNE_013.clinical_note: Pain location is the single highest-value discriminator across knee conditions

DIFF_KNE_014.text: If the pain is on the inner side of your knee, is it right at the joint line crease, or a few inches below it?

options.text: Right at the crease of the joint
A few inches below the joint crease
My pain is not on the inner side

DIFF_KNE_014.clinical_note: Joint line = meniscal/MCL; below joint line = pes anserine bursitis

DIFF_KNE_015.text: Does the pain get worse the longer you sit with your knees bent (like watching a movie)?
DIFF_KNE_015.clinical_note: Theater sign — characteristic of PFP, chondromalacia, plica syndrome

DIFF_KNE_016.text: Does the pain start after you've been running for a specific distance, and then get worse the more you run?
DIFF_KNE_016.clinical_note: Distance-dependent pain is classic ITBS pattern

DIFF_KNE_017.text: Did the pain start after a direct blow or impact to your knee or thigh?
DIFF_KNE_017.clinical_note: Direct trauma mechanism discriminates contusion from strain and overuse injuries

DIFF_KNE_018.text: Did your knee injury happen during a twisting, pivoting, or cutting movement?
DIFF_KNE_018.clinical_note: Pivoting/cutting mechanism strongly suggests ACL injury

DIFF_KNE_019.text: Is there visible swelling directly over the front of your kneecap (a soft, puffy bump)?
DIFF_KNE_019.clinical_note: Fluctuant anterior patella swelling is pathognomonic for prepatellar bursitis

DIFF_KNE_020.text: Is the pain worse when you fully straighten your knee or push it into a straight (locked) position?
DIFF_KNE_020.clinical_note: Extension pain is characteristic of Hoffa's fat pad impingement; also meniscal block

DIFF_KNE_021.text: Do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your foot or lower leg?
DIFF_KNE_021.clinical_note: Neurological symptoms below knee suggest peroneal nerve entrapment or lumbar radiculopathy

DIFF_KNE_022.text: Have you had knee surgery in the past?
DIFF_KNE_022.clinical_note: Post-surgical status essential for arthrofibrosis, tendon rupture, hardware irritation diagnoses

DIFF_KNE_023.text: Can you feel a bump or lump behind your knee that gets smaller when you bend your knee?
DIFF_KNE_023.clinical_note: Fluctuant posterior mass that changes with flexion = Baker's cyst (Foucher sign)

DIFF_KNE_024.text: Is the pain mainly worse when kneeling on the affected knee?
DIFF_KNE_024.clinical_note: Kneeling-specific pain suggests prepatellar/infrapatellar bursitis or PCL

DIFF_KNE_025.text: Are you between the ages of 10 and 15?
DIFF_KNE_025.clinical_note: Pediatric age immediately narrows to Osgood-Schlatter, Sinding-Larsen-Johansson, or osteochondral conditions

DIFF_KNE_026.text: Can you feel a tender bump on the bony point just below your kneecap, at the top of your shin bone?
DIFF_KNE_026.clinical_note: Tibial tuberosity tenderness/prominence is pathognomonic for Osgood-Schlatter in adolescents

DIFF_KNE_027.text: Is the knee stiffness constant throughout the day (not just in the morning)?
DIFF_KNE_027.clinical_note: All-day stiffness (vs morning only) suggests arthrofibrosis or advanced OA

DIFF_KNE_028.text: Did you feel the kneecap slide out of place or shift to the side during the injury?
DIFF_KNE_028.clinical_note: Patellar displacement sensation is pathognomonic for patellar dislocation/subluxation

DIFF_KNE_029.text: Did the pain come on suddenly during a kicking, jumping, or sprinting movement?
DIFF_KNE_029.clinical_note: Explosive eccentric mechanism during sport = quadriceps strain/tear

DIFF_KNE_030.text: Can you feel a gap or dent just above or just below your kneecap?

options.text: Yes, a gap ABOVE the kneecap
Yes, a gap BELOW the kneecap

DIFF_KNE_030.clinical_note: Suprapatellar gap = quad tendon rupture; infrapatellar gap = patellar tendon rupture. Highest discriminating value.

DIFF_KNE_031.text: Is the pain mainly behind your knee, deep inside?
DIFF_KNE_031.clinical_note: Deep posterior pain suggests PCL injury, Baker's cyst, or popliteal pathology

DIFF_KNE_032.text: Did you injure your knee by falling onto it while it was bent, or by hitting the front of your shin on something (like a car dashboard)?
DIFF_KNE_032.clinical_note: Posterior-directed tibial force mechanism is classic for PCL injury

DIFF_KNE_033.text: Is the pain worse when walking downhill or slowing down from a run?
DIFF_KNE_033.clinical_note: Deceleration pain is characteristic of PCL insufficiency

DIFF_KNE_034.text: Try to bend your knee and pull your heel towards your buttock with your hand. Does this cause pain in the front of the thigh?
DIFF_KNE_034.patient_guidance: Stand near a wall. Pull your heel towards your buttock gently. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_034.clinical_note: Pain on passive quad stretch with resisted extension suggests quadriceps strain or contusion

DIFF_KNE_035.text: Is there tenderness when you press on the front of your thigh (between the knee and hip)?
DIFF_KNE_035.clinical_note: Anterior thigh tenderness with swelling suggests quad strain or contusion

DIFF_KNE_036.text: Did bruising appear on your thigh 1-2 days after the injury?
DIFF_KNE_036.clinical_note: Delayed ecchymosis suggests muscle strain or contusion

DIFF_KNE_037.text: Can you feel a hard, tender lump at the spot where you were hit?
DIFF_KNE_037.clinical_note: Palpable hematoma mass at impact site is characteristic of quadriceps contusion

DIFF_KNE_038.text: Was the knee much stiffer and more painful the morning after the injury compared to right after?
DIFF_KNE_038.clinical_note: Significant day-after worsening is common with intramuscular hematoma formation

DIFF_KNE_039.text: Is the pain on the inner side of your knee worse when you stand up from a chair?
DIFF_KNE_039.clinical_note: Medial pain with sit-to-stand suggests pes anserine bursitis

DIFF_KNE_040.text: Do you kneel frequently for your work or activities (gardening, cleaning floors, etc.)?
DIFF_KNE_040.clinical_note: Occupational kneeling is the primary risk factor for prepatellar and infrapatellar bursitis

DIFF_KNE_041.text: Does the area around your knee feel warm or look red?
DIFF_KNE_041.clinical_note: Warmth + redness may indicate septic bursitis or infection — requires medical evaluation

DIFF_KNE_042.text: Is the pain on the front-inner part of your knee, just above the joint crease?
DIFF_KNE_042.clinical_note: Anteromedial pain with palpable band suggests plica syndrome

DIFF_KNE_043.text: Is there swelling just below your kneecap (on either side of the tendon that connects the kneecap to the shin)?
DIFF_KNE_043.clinical_note: Infrapatellar swelling/fullness suggests bursitis or fat pad impingement

DIFF_KNE_044.text: Is the pain worse when you stand for a long time (more than 15-20 minutes)?
DIFF_KNE_044.clinical_note: Prolonged standing pain suggests fat pad impingement (extension loading)

DIFF_KNE_045.text: Do you walk with a noticeable limp?
DIFF_KNE_045.clinical_note: Antalgic gait = pain-avoidance; steppage gait = foot drop (peroneal nerve)

DIFF_KNE_046.text: Is the pain worse with running, jumping, or kicking — and does it ease when you rest?
DIFF_KNE_046.clinical_note: Activity-related anterior knee pain in adolescents suggests SLJ or Osgood-Schlatter

DIFF_KNE_047.text: Does your kneecap appear to sit higher than normal compared to the other knee?
DIFF_KNE_047.clinical_note: Patella alta (high-riding) suggests patellar tendon rupture

DIFF_KNE_048.text: Does your knee feel stiff in every direction — both bending AND straightening — and not just in the morning?
DIFF_KNE_048.clinical_note: Global, persistent stiffness post-surgery is the hallmark of arthrofibrosis

DIFF_KNE_049.text: Is the pain at the top of your shin bone, near where a surgical plate or screws might be?
DIFF_KNE_049.clinical_note: Proximal tibial pain with hardware awareness suggests tibial plateau fracture post-op complications

DIFF_KNE_050.text: Do you have difficulty turning your foot outward, or does the front of your foot seem to drop when you walk?
DIFF_KNE_050.clinical_note: Eversion weakness with preserved inversion = peroneal nerve (not L5 root)

DIFF_KNE_051.text: Is there tenderness when you press on the bony bump on the outer side of your knee (just below the joint)?
DIFF_KNE_051.clinical_note: Fibular head tenderness suggests peroneal nerve entrapment at the fibular tunnel

DIFF_KNE_052.text: Do you also have back pain that radiates down your leg?
DIFF_KNE_052.clinical_note: Back pain with radicular leg symptoms suggests lumbar radiculopathy as pain source, not local knee pathology

DIFF_KNE_053.text: Have you noticed any swelling in your calf (below the knee)?
DIFF_KNE_053.clinical_note: Calf swelling may indicate ruptured Baker's cyst or DVT — requires medical evaluation

DIFF_KNE_054.text: When you press on the kneecap itself, is it tender?
DIFF_KNE_054.clinical_note: Patellar tenderness suggests chondromalacia, prepatellar bursitis, or patellar stress injury

DIFF_KNE_055.text: Despite having pain, can you bend and straighten your knee through its full range without it getting stuck?
DIFF_KNE_055.clinical_note: Preserved ROM with focal swelling supports bursitis over intra-articular pathology

DIFF_KNE_056.text: Try bending your knee against your other hand's resistance (like pushing against a door). Does this cause pain on the inside of the knee?
DIFF_KNE_056.patient_guidance: Sit on a chair. Place your hand behind the ankle of the painful leg. Try to bend your knee while your hand resists. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain, instability, or dizziness.
DIFF_KNE_056.clinical_note: Pain with resisted flexion at medial knee suggests pes anserine involvement
